## The question

> **Does player tracking improve completion probability beyond what
> play-by-play already knows?**

$$\Pr(\text{complete} \mid \text{game state at the throw})$$

- Measured at the instant of release, not at arrival
- Separation is a **feature of this model**, not a separate question
- Population: targeted receiver, passes beyond the line of scrimmage

::: {.notes}
"Beyond what play-by-play already knows" is the whole thesis. The next slide is
why that's a real gap.
:::

## What public models can already see

nflverse `cp`

| | |
|---|---|
| Situation | yard line, down, yards to go, home, roof, era |
| The throw | air yards, distance to sticks, air yards = 0, pass down the middle (y/n) |
| Pressure | QB hit on the play |

**Not one variable describes a defender.**

::: {.notes}
Pause here. This is the gap the project exists to fill. Source: Baldwin, Open
Source Football, 2021.
:::

## What tracking can add

At the moment of release:

| Feature | What it measures |
|---|---|
| Separation, closing speed | How open the receiver is, and whether that's changing |
| Leverage | Inside/outside, underneath/over the top |
| Passing window | Nearest defender to the ball's corridor |
| Time to arrival | Defender arrival time vs ball flight time |
| QB state | Speed, throwing across the body |

`cp` knows the pass went 14 yards down the middle. It cannot know whether the
receiver was open.

::: {.notes}
Last line is the one to say out loud.
:::

## The problem I hit

Every feature needs two points: the ball at the throw, and the ball at arrival.
The dataset ships an "arrival" label.

| | plays | completion rate |
|---|---|---|
| All thrown passes | 17,077 | **65.3%** |
| Requiring the arrival label | 14,119 | **78.3%** |

Missing on **50.6% of incompletions**, **0.8% of completions**.

Using it would have deleted half my failures and moved the base rate of the
response variable by 13 points.

::: {.notes}
Slowest slide in the deck. The filter looks like routine attrition and isn't.
Flat across all 17 weeks, so it's a labeling convention, not a collection
artifact.
:::

## Why, and the fix {.tighter}

Ball displacement per frame, relative to the catch:

| frames before | −8 | −5 | −3 | −2 | −1 | 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completions | 2.13 | 2.05 | 1.77 | 1.23 | 0.70 | 0.62 |
| Incompletions | 2.05 | 2.10 | 2.08 | 2.01 | 1.88 | 1.83 |

A ball in flight moves $\approx 2.1$ yd/frame. A ball in someone's hands moves
at running speed.

**Arrival = the last frame the ball is still flying.** Measured, not labeled,
and the rule never refers to the outcome.

*Check:* implied ball speed now agrees between completions and incompletions
within $1$ yd/s in all 11 depth bins checked, flat at $\approx 21$ yd/s.

::: {.notes}
"This table is a football being caught." Two rejected alternatives are in the
notebook if anyone asks.
:::
